title: The simplicial relative join
statement:
Use simplicial sets, products and degreewise pullbacks from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and joins and join cones from [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. Given simplicial maps $f:A\to C$ and $g:B\to C$, define
$$A\star_C B=(A\star B)\times_{C\star C}(\Delta^1\times C),$$
where the first map is $f\star g$. The map $\rho:\Delta^1\times C\to C\star C$ sends an $n$-simplex $(\epsilon,\sigma)$, with $\epsilon:[n]\to[1]$ monotone, to the ordered concatenation of the restriction of $\sigma$ to the initial $\epsilon=0$ block in the first copy and its restriction to the final $\epsilon=1$ block in the second copy. If either block is empty, use the simplex in the other copy. Faces and degeneracies are restrictions and repetitions of these ordered lists. The relative join has inclusions $i_A:A\to A\star_C B$ and $i_B:B\to A\star_C B$ over the constant parameter values $0$ and $1$. A commuting pair of maps over a base map induces the relative-join map by its maps on these pullback coordinates. In particular $C\star_C C$ identifies with $\Delta^1\times C$. For $u:A\to C$, put $A_c=A\times_C\{c\}$ and let $j_c:A_c^{\triangleright}\to A\star_C C$ be the map induced by $A_c\to A$ and $\{c\}\to C$. All objects are small in a fixed sufficiently large universe. These formulas specify data only, with no quasicategory or universal-cone assertion.
